entry.title: 31 Feline Funnies for People Raising Ruckus Cat Children
entry.summary: Some cats are just wilder than others. There are cats who can sit on your lap all day long, only taking food and bathroom breaks because they have to - and then returning to steal some more of your body warmth (and your heart). But then there are the absolute demons, the spawns of satan who were probably pspspsed here during a dark summoning ritual. My cat is not like that. Sure, she has the occasional zoomies trip in the middle of the night, but she's not the complete ruckus mess some other cats are. My friend's cat, though… he's another story completely. Way before I had a cat of my own, I took a vacation for a month, and it just so happened that this friend needed a place to stay. I sublet my room to her and her cat. She warned me he's a wacky one, and this wasn't news - I already heard the stories about him directly from her. The Prophet was his name. Well, Elijah initially, but the more character he's shown as he grew up, the more it became clear he needed his own title. So… Elijah The Prophet, yes? He's an absolute maniac. When I came back home after the sublet/vacation period, I returned to a room I did not recognize. The curtains were rolled up above the window, the computer was on the highest shelf of my closet (yes, inside), and the office chair was shredded to pieces. That was the art exhibition The Prophet left me. Or, more accurately, his hooman. The chair thing was inevitable, but the curtains and my PC were thoughtfully well-defended. But with that being said, I don't think I'm about to host that crazy cat in my house ever again. At least the story I was left with is funny, as are all this cat's other stories.

entry.title: 'To the person who loved my cat before': Person writes a heartfelt letter to their cat's previous owner who loved the cat but had to let him go to a new home
entry.summary: Rehoming a cat, sometimes, is the kindest choice. Generally, of course, we are against cats being rehomed. There are so many solutions to so many issues that can be found. Letting your cat go should always be the last choice. Because as smart as cats are, they are still just cats, and they don't understand rehoming. They just think that they were abandoned by their owners. But sometimes, when the problem is insurmountable, surrendering your cat is not only the right choice, it's also the kindest one. We always say that people should adopt a cat when they are ready, when they have enough stability in their lives. If that stability is gone, and if it can't be brought back, then you should not have a cat. It's simple to understand, but it's not easy to do. Of course, people do it all the time. We could write stories about abandoned cats every day, and we wouldn't run out. The only thing that we ask is that if you have to do it, do it right. Don't throw your indoor cat onto the street to fend for themselves. Find them another home if you can, and if you can't, take them to a shelter. So that they have an actual chance to be found by a new person who will love them just as much as you did. Like the person in today's story loves this cat.

entry.title: 20 Cats With Musical Instruments Looking Like They’re About to Drop the Album of the Year
entry.summary: Would you give a band a chance just because every member was a cat? I absolutely would. I'm in a neo-soul band, but unfortunately, none of us are cats. That would have been hilarious. In fact, we tried to make our bassist's cat part of the band, but his cat wasn't so interested. He ran away during every practice session and only came back for the food. For a big part of my life, I enjoyed music as a listener. I grew up listening to other people's songs. I went through a pop era that revolved around Justin Bieber, a punk era led by Green Day, an alternative rock era with The Strokes and Arctic Monkeys, and an emo era with My Chemical Romance. These days, I'm also a Swiftie. As you can see, my playlists have been through a lot. But I hadn't made my own music until I started playing drums and joined a band in 2021. Becoming friends with my bandmates and making songs together changed my relationship with music. So for about five years now, we've been creating our own songs, which has given me another way to enjoy music. I can try cool grooves with my friends and help turn something we're playing around with into something interesting. Musicians know that listening to your finished album is one of the most satisfactory experiences. We finally have the recorded result of all that time we spent making music together, recording, editing, producing... So after years of getting attached to other people's songs, it's nice to think that someone might discover ours and connect with them too.

entry.title: 'Happy Meowloween!': 22 Cats in Halloween Costumes Ready for a Spooktacular Party

It's a crazy thing to think about, since most cats don't like being touched or put in clothes. But there's something so cute about it that literally melts everyone's hearts. The most adorable part is that every cat looks so cute and tiny in those little clothes that fit them perfectly. Just look at the pictures I gathered below, and you'll see what I mean; it'll be impossible not to consider dressing your cat in any of these costumes this Halloween. entry.title: Your Weekly Delivery of 25 Soft and Silly Kitten Memes for a Midweek Mood Boost (October 21, 2026)
entry.summary: What is it about a tiny kitten that makes adults forget how to have a normal conversation? Why am I using my baby voice again? I can be talking about work or explaining something from class sounding like a true professional. When a kitten appears, I forget how grown-ups talk. Hiii, baby! Who's a little baby? The kitten is just sitting there while I'm asking him silly questions about why their face is so small. I do this with cat pictures, too. I can be looking at my phone and say, "Oh, look at you!" out loud while scrolling through Instagram reels. Even though there's no cat actually there to receive the compliment. It can be a stranger's kitten, but he showed up in my feed, so he's getting my compliment. He will never know this, but I don't care. He's completely unaware that I love his cute little eyes. You know that baby voice we use with our pets? Sometimes we don't even realize we've switched. Well, researchers studied it. A 2022 study found that people speak at a higher pitch when addressing cats than when talking to adults. It's called cat-directed speech. So yes, the voice I hope nobody overhears has a name and a study. And don't you feel your cat notices when you speak to them and not to someone else? That is actually real. Cats can pick up on the difference. In a small study involving 16 cats, researchers played recordings of their owners and strangers speaking. The cats distinguished between speech addressed to them and speech addressed to adults when their owner was talking, but didn't show that distinction with strangers. Isn't that sweet? Your voice means something to your cat.

entry.title: Neighbor who never saw herself as a cat person catches a mama cat and her two kittens after several months of watching them roam the block: ‘You saved 3 lives.’
entry.summary: Cat person or not, seeing stray cats in need always moves something in people's hearts. I was not always a cat person, but that changed when I started living with a cat. The cat was not mine, he officially belonged to a roommate I lived with when I was a student. This is the cat that made me warm up to cats, the previously self-described "dog person, but cats are also okay I guess". It made me love cats so much that I adopted my own cat, my beloved Cassie, whom I held in my arms for the first time when she was a month-old kitten. She's seven now, and the queen of my heart. But that's the meowgical power of cats over people. They might not be "cat people" like us - dedicated fans and feline fanatics - but their hearts are opening up to the possibility. And that's how cat people are made, just by being around cats, learning to live by their side, or seeing that they're in need. This latter option is what this one woman experienced and shared with the broader online feline family - she was not a cat person. But one mama cat and her two kittens lived outside her house for a few months, in the grueling heat, in need to be homed. It's a psychological phenomenon that works between humans too. It's called "the helper's high", and it basically describes the release of oxytocin (the bonding hormone) in our brains when we engage in prosocial behavior. That's the "high" we experience when we want to help someone, and definitely when we do help someone. And that someone can be a cat… or a cat mama and her kittens, living outside your house. And with this phenomenon, it really isn't that surprising that more people than not are becoming cat people.

entry.title: Two wholesome orange fluffy felines have a meet-cute worthy on an enemies-to-lovers movie: ‘Copper was not a fan of the new girl’
entry.summary: Have you ever tried to introduce a new cat to your current cat? Well, I've tried, and let me tell you, it's not as easy as people think. At first, you're so excited because you think, "My furbaby won't be alone anymore when I go to work; he'll have a companion!" But then you realize it's not all rosy in the garden. You see, cats are very territorial animals, whether in the wild or as one of our fluffy pets. They consider their territory their own, and they can feel threatened and feel the need to protect and defend it if another cat trespasses. Granted, not all cats are so dramatic, especially not domestic ones. In my experience, most of the time they'll just be annoyed and indifferent to the new cat for a while. Then they just start tolerating each other while pretending the other one doesn't exist. Basically, that's what I did in high school with my classmates. No wonder my boyfriend says I have the purrsonality of a cat. Either way, what happened with my cats was something along those lines. For context, my grandmother and I live next to each other, and she has a cat who loved coming to visit. She would eat here, sleep in my bed, walk around and explore the whole place, and basically treat my house as her own. But then, one day, I brought home my current cat. It was all from one day to the next, so there was no time to try an adaptation process. My grandma's cat was not happy. She didn't attack or anything; she's not aggressive, but she refuses to come inside my house now and hisses every time she sees my cat. I'm a little sad about it, but I still get to see her when walking in the yard, when I go to Grandma's house, and I know she's well taken care of. In this case, we have an orange furball named Copper, who suddenly got an unexpected companion. Let's just say it'll take a while for him to process everything.

entry.title: Giant ginger cat built like a retired wrestler rules over Japanese cat café with an iron paw, until one visitor who just came in for coffee wins his heart and gets handed adoption papers
entry.summary: When a cat adopts you, resistance is futile. Especially if it's a gigantic orange cat that bites French people. I have mixed feelings about cat cafés. On the one hand, I love having a place outside my own home where I can be surrounded by cats, and on the other hand, I feel bad for them. The good news is that cat cafés have improved a lot in the last couple of years. When they first started, they were basically a petting zoo for cats. No one really cared for the cats' needs, as they were merely a means to bring customers into the café. Now, the purpose of most of these cafés is for cat adoption instead of being entertainment for people while they dine or sip on a cup of mediocre coffee. Of course, there are still some cafés that use them as a tool, so always do your research before visiting a cat (or any animal) café. Sometimes, people go there for the purrpose of finding a cat to adopt, while others, like the visitor in our "story" today from Japan, actually end up getting adopted. Simply coming in for a cup of coffee, they were warned about a purrmanently grumpy orange cat who had serious cattitude. He was notorious for knocking drinks off of tables and apparently biting French people. How he knew they were French, we have no idea, but apparently, he knew. After a fair amount of warning, the menacing ginger cat actually climbed into their lap and started purring. Needless to say, the staff were shocked. They demanded the visitor take him home, even to the point of practically shoving adoption papers into their hands before leaving. Even if this story is a well-written joke, there's still a lesson in there that we could all take home with us: don't judge cats by their appearances. Some of the "grumpiest" cats I've ever met have been the biggest snuggle bugs as soon as they meet their purrson and find a place they finally feel safe. And, as always, when a cat chooses you, your fate has already been decided for you. That's just the way the Cat Distribution System works.

entry.title: 22 Spooky Season Cat Memes for a Purranormal Dose of Feline Fun
entry.summary: Trick or treat! The magic words to get strangers to open their doors to you and give you free candy. Cats trick or treat too, they just don't always tell you they're going out on the town. In honor of Halloween coming in the next few days, here at I Can Has Cheezburger, we're celebrating all month with dressed up, costumed out, cool, spooky kitties who just want some free salmon snacks. Cats have the most intimate relationship with Halloween, and not just black void cats either! There's nothing a cat loves more than to be snuggled up in soft blankets and covers, fireplace rolling, a Halloween movie on in the background while their pet loving owner cuddles them to kitty dreamland. So if you're a Halloween guy or gal with a feline friend, just know they're celebrating too! Halloween is my favorite holiday. I know, I know, it's a bit kitschy for fake goths or people still obsessed with Tim Burton films well into their 50s, but who said there's anything wrong with kitsch? Even if you're a 50-year-old whose phone background is Nightmare Before Christmas, it's simply important to celebrate the things that make you feel you. And for a lot of people, it's the whole spooky season, in which Halloween exists in. We're not the only ones enjoying spooky season; there's a whole society of cats celebrating witch hunts, dressing up, and doing seances behind closed doors. These adorable, yet spooky dressed up cat memes are the purrfect medicine for a bad day, or the inspiration you needed to get into the holiday spirit. There's something ethereal about the autumn and everything it encompasses. The grey skies, the possibility of rain, the brisk air, and the wind pushing stray leaves to and froe. So enjoy scrolling these cats in costume while you prep for Halloween.

entry.title: 24 Cute Cat Memes to Fall Into the Sweet Spooky Season With (October 20, 2026)
entry.summary: What do you do with all your Halloween decorations after the spooky season is over? All good things come to an end, and the spooky season is not far from its own end. Sure, Halloween is still ahead of us, and we still haven't gone trick-or-treating and filled our bags with a year's worth of candy, yet most of October is already behind us, so we are starting to prepare for the end of fall and the beginning of something new. Which brings me back to the question: what do you do with all your fall and Halloween decorations? Some people have plenty of storage room where they can pack everything up in a box and leave it to rest until next year. The Jack-o'-lanterns, skeletons, costumes, and every single home decor item that matches the color theme of fall go into that box. It's a very efficient way to ensure you have everything you need this time next year, without having to spend any more money. Those of us who don't have enough storage room, however, need to find other solutions to all that decoration, so they won't have to spend the next 10 months staring at Halloween decorations that have no business being there. So we stick them in a random room, continue to use fall-scented candles well into December, and find creative solutions for the random decorative pumpkins we put around the house.

entry.title: A Silly Soirée of 28 Dapper Tuxedo Cats Whose Mustaches Demand to Be Taken Seriously
entry.summary: Gather round, ladies, gents, and silly cat people - it's mustache time. I'm not sure what makes a cat's fur pattern unique, because every cat is different from one another, but I do know this - the rarer the phenomenon, the more special it looks in our human eyes. For cats looking at other cats it matters exactly zero percent of what it matters to us. They recognize each other by smell, meow pitch, and other parameters - but special fur features? They leave this visual distinction and admiration for us humans. But despite the fact that every cat is unique because of their character, it's still fun to look at the rare fur colors cats sport. For example, brown cats are so rare that there's no official data anywhere to determine the percentage of the brown cat population worldwide. And don't even let me start about the cat with a mohawk I saw once - he's such a rockstar with his unique fur alone! So I want to welcome you to this silly soirée of another rare phenomenon happening on dapper tuxedo cats - their impurressive mustaches.

entry.title: Woman opens her doors for a breeze during Super El Niño and thinks her heat migraine caused her to see double: ‘Nope, it’s an actual second cat looking like our cat.’
entry.summary: Super El Niño is rough on animals just as it is on humans, but luckily for cats, they tend to adopt themselves into safety. When the weather is extreme, cats need shelter. Strays need shelter, period. But when the weather becomes way too much, it's important that cats stay in a safe space until things calm down outside, whether from the cold or the heat. And that's especially true for when we feel the bad weather ourselves - if we're cold, they're cold. If we're hot, they're hot. And if a Super El Niño ravages the Pacific, it doesn't affect only humans. And people really do feel its effects as we speak - severe droughts, massive floods, and record-breaking global heat. This is serious. But even amidst this serious event, a little silliness shines its light. And of course, no wonder it has to do with cats. One woman experiencing the effects of this current Super El Niño also experiences migraines - which is an annoying thing in and of itself. But some migraines are so strong they can affect your eyesight - which is exactly what she thought was happening when she saw her cat just doubled. But cats being cats, you probably already guessed this was not her eyesight making her see double. This was a cat identical to hers who simply sought a safe space from the extreme heat outside. It's a Cat Distribution System thing - to send people a secret twin of their resident cat to make them softer for the idea of adopting them. It's a secret matchmaking technique the CDS employs, with great success. Even I took in a kitten who was identical to my cat just because he reminded me how tiny and helpless my cat was as a kitten who needed to be adopted. I was a foster for him, and he eventually went to a wonderful forever home, but the idea is similar.

entry.title: Shelter cat Bruce finally has a forever home and spends his first night purring before falling asleep hugging his human’s foot: 'I've never seen a happier cat'
entry.summary: Do you know what a home is? Bruce's new human asked him that question, and it made me think about how I would answer. Watching the newly adopted cat purr through his first night home and fall asleep hugging his human's foot made me think of the relief I feel when I'm tired and know I have somewhere familiar to come back to. Even before I get there, thinking about home helps. To me, home means a future. It gives me the stability to think beyond the day. I know I have somewhere safe to sleep tonight, so that leaves room to consider what I want for myself tomorrow. I can start something, leave it unfinished, and come back to it. I can make plans knowing I have a place to build them from. I get the feeling of "home" even when I'm not there. On the way home, I begin thinking about making dinner, putting on something comfortable, and settling in for the evening. I'm lucky to know where I'm going to sleep. I know I can close the door and stay. Reaching the end of a day and having a place where I can let myself feel whatever I've been holding in feels reassuring.

entry.title: 69-year-old man and 11-year-old shy rescued lion have been best friends since he was a cub, now they cuddle at night, ride trucks together, and go on walks side by side

And today, a new story to add to the list, a new person to be jealous of- sorry, to admire. Meet Frikkie Von Solms, a 69-year-old man, and Zion, the 11-year-old rescued lion who is his best friend.

entry.title: 'She walked right into my arms': I thought I'd lost my newly adopted kitten forever, then she came home 24 hours later in a moment I'll never forget
entry.summary: If your cat runs away, don't lose hope too quickly. As a cat owner of a very lazy, very spoiled house cat, one of my worst nightmares is my cat running away. Because I know her. And I know she won't make it. Our trips to the vet are something awful. The moment she is out of the house, she starts making noises she never makes otherwise - screaming like those stray cats in fights that we hear outside sometimes. She only likes the outside when it's on the other side of a window. Then, she's happy. Loves watching birds, loves listening to the sound of cars, loves sniffing the fresh, crispy air. 24 hours would be the longest she would make it outside. Then, she would come back. And that's not just a guess, or a joke. I know that for a fact. Because it happened. There is no lesson to this story. I was lucky that she found her way back to me after 24 hours, and I'll tell you exactly how amazing and unlikely that was in a moment. If there is anything that I would like you to take away from this story, it's this: If your cat runs away, don't give up. Keep looking for them. Keep listening. For as long as you can handle it. Often, they want to come back. But they might need a little help finding their way.

entry.title: The Story Behind Amsterdam's Floating Cat Shelter, Where Rescued Cats Find a Home on the Water

Now my question is: why are we tourists visiting the Van Gogh Museum and not this shelter? I would have gone straight there if I knew about it. The works of art are of a different kind, but still, I bet tourists walk out of the place equally astonished by the cuteness. According to its official history, it all started back in 1966 when a woman named Henriette van Weelde found a mother cat and her kittens beneath a tree opposite her home. She took them in, and more cats followed, including animals whose owners could no longer care for them. She was soon recognized as the "cat lady" in the neighborhood. Two years later, she was running out of room for the animals, so she came up with the coolest idea ever: buying a boat for the cats so they could live there. Yes, she bought an old Dutch sailing barge and turned it into a cat shelter. If people can live in boats, why can't cats? Some volunteers joined her, and the Catboat Foundation became official.

entry.title: Cat lover who’s very allergic to cats adopts a dog, and on a daily walk she leads her to the one cat who doesn’t set off her allergies: 'Welcome home, Willow.'
entry.summary: What are the chances you'll meet the absolutely right cat for you to adopt? Being allergic to cats is tough. Not just when you walk down the street and a cute stray wants your attention, and not just when you visit a house of friends or family and they have a cat inside. It's especially tough when you actually love cats. That's how my wife is - she's allergic to cats, officially. She grew up with cats from early childhood. When her mom told her not to let the cat sleep in the same bed with her, she snuggled even closer to the cat, took a big whiff, and called it "exposure therapy". It took her two childhood cats and living with mine for a few years to stop having symptoms. So… success. But that's not the case for every allergic person. Some carry this throughout all their lives, or at least think they're going to take this massive hindrance to giving cats love to the grave with them. But here below we have a woman, a cat lover like us, who's allergic to cats. So much so that she's never had one proper. And what do cat people who are allergic to cats do? That's right, adopt a dog. A small one, preferably, so it's as close to a cat as possible. That, for instance, can't happen with my wife - she's afraid of dogs. But that's a story for another time. And this woman from below here? She did do just that. But you see, the Cat Distribution System works in mysterious ways. It doesn't just distribute the cats who need a home to people who will take them in - it makes sure the right cat goes to the right person. And it really does all of that matchmaking in mysterious ways, hidden from our eyes. And behind the scenes, the Cat Distribution System sometimes employs dogs as agents. That's right - a dog cat adopts the cat for you, or at least leads you to the cat you're supposed to adopt. So you might ask, "What are the chances you'll meet the cat who's just right for you?" Well, with a dog agent of the CDS, very high. Even if you're "insanely allergic to cats"…

entry.title: Teh Hisstory of LOLcats: How silly kitties conquered the internet, one cheezburger at a time
entry.summary: Unless you're a veteran Cheezburger lover from pre-2007, you've probably heard us throw around the term "LOLcats" before, but do you know where it really comes from? Welcome to our I Can Has Cheezburger hisstorian's guide to the rise of feline royalty. Gather 'round, fellow feline fanatics, meme meowsters, and distinguished scholars of the ancient art of catposting. Today, we're dusting off our internet archives and embarking on a journey through one of the most impawtant cultural movements of the digital age: the rise of the LOLcat. Listen up, youth! Yes, there was a time before TikTok and Instagram. We were the "go play outside and don't come back in unless one of you is hurt" generation. Then, somewhere along the way, computers were introduced, and we even had computer classes in school. The internet was young, the pixels were plentiful, and the spelling was absolutely atrocious. We're talking, of course, about the glorious era of "I CAN HAS CHEEZBURGER?" We can't just give our thanks to the first meme creators, but we definitely will later in this article. My goal in this awwducational anthology is to show you that our LOLcats history goes much further back than the age of the internet, and how many steps were taken to get to the meowdern meme culture we have today. Those reaction memes you save and send to your friends or coworkers are there because of a rich history of people being obsessed with their cats. Get comfy - it's time we begin.

entry.title: Kitty falls down from the docks, swims struggling to go back to shore, and kind hoomans go out of their way to rescue him and bring it back to firm land
entry.summary: Everybody knows that cats don't usually like water, but sometimes they can't get away from it, no matter how hard they try… We've all seen those videos of dogs in summer, swimming happily in their hooman's pools. They look like they're having the time of their life, and we're rooting for them! But with cats, that is rarely ever the case. There's a reason why most people don't give baths to their cats on a regular basis, and that's mainly because they don't react well. The cat can end up getting stressed out, and we can get a few bites and scratches as our war scars. This doesn't necessarily mean that all cats hate water, or that you'll never be able to give your furbaby a bath even if they come home completely dirty. It just means that we need to be more careful with the way we approach the whole cat-water issue, since some of them might be scared of what water means. I've mentioned before that my cat is a rescue, and the first time they brought her home, she was covered in dirt from head to toe. She needed to get a bath, since she couldn't be in the house all dirty. At first we thought she was just a grey cat, but after the bath, we found out that she was actually black and white! A bath was definitely necessary after all. That first time, she reacted well. She seemed to be too scared to try to do anything, but now, I can't be sure how she would react. Mind you, she's getting dangerously close to needing another bath. She spends a lot of time running around and hiding behind and under furniture, so yes, she comes out all covered in dust quite often, and although I get her clean as best as I can, I might find myself in need of scheduling another bath soon. In this case, it wasn't that the cat was escaping from bath time; nope: the poor thing fell out of the docks and into the sea, and was desperately trying to swim back to shore.

entry.title: Person catches neighbor in the act of throwing their cat into the trash, stops them, adopts the cat, reports them, and turns the neighbor's trash into their most precious treasure
entry.summary: When you get a chance to right a wrong, would you take it? It is easy to say that you would step in and do the right thing if you saw someone doing something bad. For cats? Innocent creatures? We would do anything! Right? It's so easy to say that. But when push comes to shove, when you actually have to face something like that, to confront someone doing bad… would you? If we had been regular people on the internet, seeing all of these viral stories, maybe we would have lost hope. But we're not. We're cat content curators, and we are very happy to say that some people actually do intervene in these moments. Some of my personal favorite examples are the 8-year-old kid who saved a cat from a bunch of other kids who were hurting it by trading his skateboard for the kitten. Another example is the group of coworkers who banded together to save their boss's kitten from neglect. Another is all the people who have watched cats be thrown out of moving car windows and stopped their own car to save the desperate cat. And in today's story, a person actively caught their neighbor in the act of throwing their cat into the trash. Confrontation in a situation like that is risky, and it's scary, but it was worth it. This person saved the cat, adopted the cat, and reported the neighbor. And things feel a little more right in the world.
